title: The True Theology of Abraham
english: Many waters are brought forth in vain, through which the impious and godless contend. For they wish to imitate through them the one who said, 'If anyone thirsts, let him come to me and drink, and whoever drinks of the water I will give him shall become a spring of water welling up to eternal life' (John 4:14). And indeed, in these things Jesus gives as if it were one water; this is the Spirit which those believing in him are to receive.

The waters of the heterodox, through which they imitate the quenching given by the Lord, are many, because they are diverse and discordant and do not lead to a single end; for both the ends and the beginnings of their mindsets are different. 'Send therefore,' says the Psalmist, 'your poetic and protective hand, to bring me out and to rescue me from many waters and from the hand of strange sons' (Ps 143:7). For the strange is commonly to be taken both in terms of sons and of waters. And it is possible to say that to be rescued from many waters means from the evil powers and from the devil, the king of all those in such waters; and to be rescued from the hand of strange sons means those working through men.

The ten-stringed psaltery is composed and joined by the energy of the ten commandments; for each of the ten commandments is a string musically composed in the whole instrument. 'And kings, he says, you shall perceive, and those who rule perceptibly the nations and the inhabited world' (Ps 143:10). For if a king is not saved by much power, the kings being saved by God possess the kingdom. And also it is said of giving salvation to kings. Since they always have it from the one being saved, he did not cease to give salvation, but always has given, and will give, and gives. And the same applies concerning the one redeeming and not having redeemed and the one about to redeem.

Be useful to those destined for the turning away of the world (Ps 143:12). For concerning the women of the church, Paul writes how they, praying with modesty and self-control, adorn themselves with the works of godliness, but not with the laying down of gold and pearls and elaborate hairstyles (1 Tim 2:9). Consider these things said and apply them to the heterodox. For their word is struck like swords.

Regarding the devouring and the stripping away of those who have not put on the armor of God. Those previously mentioned as speaking vanity, who are alien sons, use this evil sword. The divine thoughts may be their sons, having strength in youth but not in perfection, being like their daughters, whose words are beautified and trimmed with a smooth composition and the elegance of phrasing.

Therefore, they are a likeness of a temple but not a temple; for they do not have within themselves a divine mind like the words of the divine Scriptures; for a temple is where God is found in them who encounter them rightly. He exalts God, the one theologizing rightly and truly, uttering great and high things concerning God (Ps 144:1). He says regarding the faith set forth of him who became a child of Abraham through works and faith, that the God of all causes is not [his God], but he confesses toward him, 'I am your God.' But he, having become a man of God by serving his God, fleeing every evil kingdom, is ruled by this God himself, and so he will be able to say, 'You are my king and my God.' Having the soul say immortal, he says, 'I will bless your name for ever and unto the age of ages.' And he blesses the name of God and his king, the one doing to wear it and saying and thinking the things belonging to the divine calling upon him, beginning to bless from the present age unto the doing of it as of the age; for if now, knowing in part and participating partially in the good, he blesses the name of the benefactor, much more he will bless when he approaches the perfect good and the face-to-face knowledge of God.

And it shall be said also concerning those from the circumcision and from the Gentiles who have believed: 'Generation and generation shall praise your works' (Ps 144:4), being rightly worthy of praise by his own word, just as he has seen the divine Creator with a divine gaze to be very beautiful. The holiness of God is not another of the Savior; for he himself is the sanctification who sanctifies those approaching God, to whom it is said, 'You shall be holy, as I am holy' (Lev 11:44). The glory of this holiness is majestic.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Kingship of God and the Justice of His Son
english: It is. Therefore, those who have been instructed in the holiness of God and also in his glory, they are transformed and they hymn him magnificently, not by bare speech, but before this by works and right disposition, thinking, acting, and speaking holily, gloriously, and magnificently.

The glory of the holiness of God is able to be: 'He will glorify' (that is, the Paraclete), what he will take from me and declare to you. Therefore, also those who hear him declaring, in giving the word of wisdom and the word of knowledge, they speak of this holiness. And toward this they will recount his wonders, not merely what the holiness is, but penetrating the mystical word of his wonders, which occur at various times and are occurring, with precision and keen contemplation.

It is fearful to fall into the hands of the living God (Hebrews 10:31), and 'Shout to God with a voice of joy' (Ps 144:6), what the Lord is most high and awesome; they will say this in practice and through right understanding (for through this fear of God and exceeding reverence, they will say to him the power of his awesome things). And if they have been benefited, they will fear his greatness with virtue and sinlessness, and they will not say 'the power of your awesome things' but they will recount it after having known what is without experience and without limit; for they do not recount it as having described and limited it to the intellect, but as surpassing every human apprehension.

For only the Son knows who the Father is, and the Father who the Son is; but even if the Son reveals the Father as he wills, not as it is possible for humans to see according to analogy, anyone who has it before preparation will make him manifest. Since a perceptible trembling becomes a fullness (for having been filled with food, he sends out spirits bringing breath, according to the quality of the things eaten), it follows that one must say that he who has eaten the words concerning the goodness of God, having been filled from these spiritual foods, intensely stirs up the memory of the goodness of God, of the goodness capable of being good. But since it is advantageous toward knowing God for the good, also his justice...

And the mind judges them, so that the memory of your goodness shall be searched out, and they shall rejoice in your justice. The justice of God can be the only-begotten offspring of Him, upon which those having obtained the Wisdom born to us from God—justice and sanctification and redemption—rejoice.

For what was sent to proclaim to the captives the goodness of God has become redemption for those being set free from captivity, who, remembering the goodness of God that happened to them, search out its memory; but also having perceived how they were justified, it having become for them the work of the one redeeming and of the justice from God, they rejoice in this justice of God. And those who are to receive both all practical virtue and the justice having come through the faith of Jesus into all those believing are made manifest in the present word. [Ps 144:13] All those whom God has made through his word and his wisdom, God holds and reigns; therefore God is almighty.

Since, therefore, even the ages, being part of all things, have come to be through God by means of the Savior according to the Scripture saying, 'Through whom also he made the ages, and over all of them he reigns,' and since the thing theologized by Paul agrees with these things: 'To the King of the ages, the incorruptible, invisible, only wise God' [1 Tim 1:17]. For to reign over all the ages and to be the King of the ages is the same thing.

Consider if it is said of the Son, 'Your kingdom is the kingdom of all the ages,' reigning over Jacob, that his kingdom has no end; for reigning over all those having come through him, he holds and reigns for the ages. Therefore, just as the others who belong to the Father, so also the Almighty shares in the approachability. If not the Father is the King of the ages and the Son's kingdom is the kingdom of all the ages, it is fitting that his kingdom is also without beginning and without end, both before the ages and while reigning with them; for 'the Lord reigns for an age and for ever and ever' [Ps 10:16], and 'our God is King before an age,' that is, before every age. Accordingly, his lordship also extends to the kingship...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: True Calling and the Divine Will
english: He rules over all generations, being Lord of those within time and generation, but reigning over those who have ascended beyond the temporal by looking at the unseen and eternal things. 'But God is faithful in all his words' (Ps 144:13a). It is said not that they offer [something] from faith or by faith, but that it is fitting for the one who believes.

Indeed, everything he says becomes according to what is written: 'He said, and he will not do or speak, and he will not remain' [text is garbled/corrupt here]. For it is said, 'Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will never pass away' (Matt 24:35). Regarding being faithful in his words and holy in all his works, imparting to them the holiness from himself: just as one is holy among those participating in his holiness, and the Savior is wise among the wise according to him, so the Lord is holy in all his works becoming holy through communion with him.

Perhaps those who are in desires and bad thoughts without practice fall; but those who sin actively are shattered. However, he helps both sides, supporting some and restoring others. How does he support? By commanding each one, 'You shall not covet your neighbor's wife' (Ex 20:17), and the following, and 'Do not let beauty's desire overcome you' (Prov 21:9) by advising through a wise man. Those falling are those sinning in morals while being encompassed by Christianity, but those shattered are those turning away from it; those falling are those sinning in practice, but those shattered are those who embrace impious heresies of the ungodly.

In all his ways he causes to walk, providing and governing, judging, benefiting, granting, punishing; righteous he is found (Ps 144:17a); 'for God is faithful, and there is no injustice' (Ps 144:17). If someone says his ways are the virtues (for those traveling practically and intellectually bring them to him), and in these he appears righteous. No one living earnestly and according to virtue blames providence, but if someone has stood foolishly outside his ways: 'A man's folly ruins his paths' (Prov 14:12), yet he blames God in his heart. Regarding the saying of 'ways' and those given from him in...

If one dares, the righteous man will be known, having matched them in power to those who have received [grace]. But he who says that nature is an unproven virtue in men, or that fate is forcing them into sin, does not rightly say that God is in the ways He has legislated (Ps 144,18).

It is said that He is near to those who call upon His name. Therefore, those making progress pass on to calling upon Him in truth; for calling upon the name of the Lord is more introductory for those who are perfecting themselves in calling Him. For Moses says, and Aaron among His priests, and Samuel among those calling His name, they called upon the Lord, and He himself heard them—those doing this sincerely and not by chance.

It is possible to say that those living according to the letter of the law call upon the name of the Lord, whereas those following the novelty of the Spirit call upon Him in truth, appropriately worshiping Him in spirit and truth. Each of those having a pious disposition, having denied human will, wishes to have the will of God, saying, 'Teach me to do your will, O my God, for You are God' (Ps 51:17). Therefore, he who does the will of those fearing Him transforms his own will into action, he who wishes to have God as his will, revering Him.

And there is no difference, in the plural or the singular, between 'wills' and 'the will'; for His wills are the virtues according to each kind, but His will in general is the universal and common virtue. He who wishes to be guarded by Him, so that by no means the evil one may deceive him, let him love God with all his heart and soul and strength. To those thus guarded by Him because they love Him, the things promised without falsehood are made favorable, concerning which it has been said, 'An eye has not seen and an ear has not heard, nor has there risen upon the heart of man [what] God has prepared for those who love Him' (Ps 144,19a).

He says 'mouth,' not the sensible but the intelligible, as also in another psalm toward God: 'I will open my lips, and my mouth shall declare your praises.' Yet, when His praises are being spoken, all flesh having heard Him shall bless His holy name.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
